title: Smiths "Deluxe" ref 6B/542 Military Watch for the British RAF
description: In the late 1940s and early 1950s, Smiths was commissioned to produce a General Service wristwatch for the British Armed Forces. The British government, concerned about dependence on foreign watch suppliers—something that had proven problematic during World War II—offered Smiths substantial contracts to encourage domestic watch production. However, for reasons unknown, the British Army ultimately chose not to move forward with the order. It wasn’t until the late 1960s that Smiths secured a military contract—this time for the W10 model. These watches were assigned the same 6B/542 stores reference as the Omega navigators’ watch, suggesting they were likely issued to RAF pilots and navigators. This is the rarest Smiths British military watch, and arguably one of the rarest British military watches of all. Approximately 300 of these watches were made and issued to the RAF in 1954, 1955, and 1956—presumably as a test order. This would make sense for a trial run, as the inside of an aircraft cockpit presented a challenging environment for mechanical wristwatches, mainly due to the presence of electromagnetic fields. To combat this, the watches were equipped with an iron dial and a metal dust cover, which together created an effective Faraday cage to shield the movement from electromagnetic interference. This particular Smiths was issued in 1955, as evidenced by its issue number on the case back. The case is in lovely condition, with fixed bars for fitting a single-pass strap—so military personnel had a slimmer chance of losing the watch during duties. This example has been fully serviced by our watchmaker and is ready for new adventures in the years to come. A fun fact about these Smiths Deluxe watches: there were also some non-issued, non-military-marked versions. This particular model, housed in a water-resistant case, was worn by Sir Edmund Hillary during his ascent of Everest (and you thought it was all about Rolex!). The Smiths De Luxe A454 and A460 models, known as the ‘Antarctic’ versions, were supplied to the 1957 British Antarctic expedition, in which Hillary also participated. These models feature a silver-colored dial and a finer outer minute track. These super RARE purpose-built watches hold real history and have a super cool wrist presence, we think. Get in touch! title: IWC Da Vinci Perpetual Calendar Silver Dial Ref. IW375803
description: The IWC Da Vinci line emerged in 1969 with the introduction of the very first IWC Da Vinci, equipped with the infamous Beta 21 quartz movement. However, the watch we have at hand is a very different kind of timepiece! The first significant evolution of the collection occurred in 1985 with what is undoubtedly the most famous version: the Da Vinci Perpetual Calendar (Ref. 3750). This model was created under the technical guidance of Kurt Klaus, while Günter Blümlein served as CEO of IWC. The launch of this watch is quite significant, and the context warrants explanation. During the early 1980s, the Swiss watch industry faced massive changes. Interest in quality mechanical timepieces—ranging from simple three-hand watches to complex pieces—was limited to a small group of collectors and enthusiasts. Wearers of mechanical watches were rare and often perceived as “old-school” or “outdated.” While sales representatives from historic brands like IWC attempted to convey the beauty of mechanical movements and the dedication of watchmakers in crafting fine timepieces, clients were captivated by the slim and precise electronic quartz watches. At the Basel Watch Fair in 1985, a new watch was introduced that combined striking design with a complex perpetual calendar chronograph movement (the ancestor of the watch we have today): the Da Vinci Perpetual Calendar (Ref. 3750). This watch, the first in the new Da Vinci collection, is the result of designer Hano Burtscher’s vision, featuring a round design with articulated swivel lugs. More importantly, this watch symbolizes the resurgence of complex mechanical movements. At the end of the 1970s, Kurt Klaus developed a perpetual calendar module that allowed all settings to be made via the crown, easily attachable to almost any movement—from a simple three-hander to a chronograph. Our watch is based on this design language and movement, featuring a nicely sized 41mm steel case with “mushroom” pushers. There is a lot to take in when looking at the dial: it features a white background with painted Arabic numeral hour markers, a 12-hour chronograph, a perpetual calendar displaying the day, date, month, and four-digit year, as well as a moonphase! All of this is protected by a sapphire crystal. The moonphase has a lovely sparkle, a little detail we truly appreciate. All settings can be adjusted using the crown at 3 o’clock—a very ingenious design! This lovely IWC comes on a Bulang & Sons strap and has been fully serviced by our watchmaker. We believe this is a steal at this price—just look at what you're getting in this range. Let's get a great deal done! title: Blancpain Fifty Fathoms 3H Bundeswehr

You will notice this watch doesn't look like your stereotypical Blancpain Fifty Fathoms, due to the bezel insert. The Bund divers were using re breathers so didn’t need the gradiated dive bezels we know from Rolex Subs and so the insert was plain , without numerals.. It is very unusual to find one of these watches in good and original condition, especially the bakelite bezel . This one cracked at the tritium triangle at 12 , so it actually is a proof of use as intended- the bakelite under the triangle is almost not existent so this is were they all crack normally ! The 41mm case is very strong all-round and has fixed strap bars and a winding crown at five o’clock. The case back has the Bund engraving: 6645 -12-4162. The original hands contain tritium lume ( with some “military life on them “ ) that are good match with the hour plots, which are tritium as denoted by the 3H on the dial. We really love the funky orange minute hand ! Coming on the photographed Nato strap. The Automatic movement has been fully checked and regulated by our watch maker . Finding examples like this in this condition is not easy, this is a very special watch indeed, please get i touch to get this tool vibe wrapped around your wrist ! We love issued watches and this is a great find. Let’s talk and do a deal! title: Rolex GMT-Master 1675 MK1 Long-E Dial Fuchsia Insert with Box and Accessories
description: The Rolex GMT-Master was introduced in 1955 to solve a practical challenge of the emerging jet age: enabling commercial pilots to track two time zones simultaneously. Developed in collaboration with Pan American World Airways (Pan Am), it quickly became an indispensable navigation tool for long-haul crews and international travellers alike. Over the decades, the GMT-Master evolved from a purpose-built aviation instrument into one of the world's most iconic sports watches. While its unmistakable design has changed remarkably little, it remains the definitive travel watch—combining rugged functionality with timeless style. Presented here is a wonderful 1970 example, featuring the first-generation matte dial—arguably the most desirable of them all. Collectors refer to it as the "Long E" or Mark I dial, named after the elongated middle stroke of the "E" in the Rolex logo, a detail unique to this early execution. The case is in beautiful condition, even retaining its original green caseback sticker—always a pleasure to see after more than five decades. Equally impressive is the original "Pepsi" bezel insert, which has developed the highly sought-after "Fuchsia" coloration, where the red half has taken on a vibrant pinkish-purple hue. For years, collectors have debated whether these inserts left the Rolex factory in this colour or gradually developed it over time. Interestingly, the reverse side of this insert displays the same fuchsia tone, strongly suggesting the colour is original rather than the result of sun exposure. To make things even more convincing, we own an original Rolex brochure illustrating a GMT-Master fitted with an insert in exactly this shade. We like to think this one was simply born a Fuchsia. The Mark I matte dial is equally impressive, displaying beautifully preserved tritium lume with a warm creamy-yellow patina that perfectly complements the colours of the bezel. The watch is fitted with its folded Oyster bracelet, reference 7836, with 258 end links and a clasp stamped 1/71. And there's more. Accompanying the watch is an outstanding and remarkably complete set of original accessories, including the Rolex cardboard outer box, the rare "coffin" style inner box, the red seal card, booklets, green document holder, polishing cloth, and the original Rolex UK guarantee booklet, which remains unfilled. A fantastic GMT-Master, a coveted Fuchsia bezel, and a remarkably complete set—this is exactly the kind of vintage Rolex we love. If this one doesn't make you smile, we don't know what will. title: Rolex Cosmograph Daytona 116520 Panna dial Box and Paper Set
description: The Rolex Daytona is one of the most iconic chronographs in watchmaking history. Its story spans more than six decades and is closely tied to motor racing, technical innovation, and collector culture. The "Panna" dial is among the rarest and most coveted variations of the stainless steel Rolex Daytona reference 116520. Its nickname is derived from the Italian word for "cream," inspired by the dial's distinctive warm ivory tone. Originally produced as a bright white dial, a subtle imperfection in the varnish caused a small number of examples to naturally develop this beautiful creamy patina over time. These dials are almost exclusively found in watches produced between 2000 and 2003. Unlike the celebrated "tropical" dials of vintage Rolex models, which gradually turn brown, the Panna dial evolves into a soft, even cream color, giving each watch its own unique character. Today, the Panna dial is considered one of the most collectible modern Rolex dial variations, representing one of the last documented instances of a naturally occurring production anomaly resulting in a distinct dial color. Offered here is an exceptional P-series example from 2000, placing it within this highly desirable production window. The watch remains in outstanding condition, featuring a strong, well-preserved case with sharp lugs, an unpolished tachymeter bezel, and a beautifully aged cream dial with an even, attractive patina. The watch is fitted with its correct Oyster bracelet, reference 78490, featuring solid end links and a clasp stamped "DT4." The movement has been fully serviced by our watchmaker and is running exactly as it should. Further enhancing its collectability, this Daytona is accompanied by its original punched guarantee paper, confirming its original sale in Mexico, along with the inner presentation box, both booklets, the 2001/2002 calendar, and the original calendar holder. Smooth, rare, and impossible to ignore—just like panna cotta. Get in touch! title: Rolex Cosmograph Daytona 6265 MK2 Silver Sigma Panda Dial
description: Few watches in modern horology carry the same cultural significance and collector appeal as the Rolex Cosmograph Daytona. While Rolex has created an extraordinary catalogue of icons—including the Submariner, Datejust, and Explorer—the Daytona has achieved a near-mythical status. Once readily available through authorised retailers, the stainless steel Daytona gradually became one of the most difficult sports watches to acquire. Long before today's infamous waiting lists, demand consistently exceeded supply, cementing its place as one of the most coveted modern Rolex references. Today, securing a stainless steel Daytona through official channels is often a prolonged and uncertain process, yet its appeal remains undiminished. For many owners, it represents far more than a timepiece; it is a tangible connection to motorsport history, mechanical precision, and decades of continuous refinement. Interestingly, the Daytona's legendary status was far from guaranteed. When first introduced, it was a relatively slow seller and would take decades before collectors fully appreciated its significance. Its story began with Rolex's early chronograph development in the early 1960s, culminating in the introduction of the Cosmograph in 1963. By 1964, the name "Daytona" started appearing on certain dials, giving birth to the identity we know today. The term "Cosmograph" itself remains somewhat unusual within watchmaking. While "chronograph" derives from the Greek chronos (time) and graph (to write)—a reference to early timing instruments such as Nicolas Rieussec's 19th-century invention that physically recorded elapsed time—"Cosmograph" feels broader and more aspirational, reflecting Rolex's ambition to elevate the chronograph beyond a simple timing instrument. The name "Daytona," by contrast, is much easier to understand. It directly reflects the watch's motorsport DNA. During the 1960s, Daytona Beach was regarded as one of the most prestigious racing venues in American motorsport, and in 1966 Rolex became the official timekeeper of the Daytona International Speedway. From that moment onward, the "Daytona" name began appearing alongside "Cosmograph" on the dial, although not always consistently across early production examples. title: Rolex Turn- o-graph Silver linen dial ref 1625
description: For those newer to Rolex, the name Turn-O-Graph might not immediately ring a bell. Discontinued in 2011, it no longer appears in the Rolex catalogue and was often overshadowed by models like the Daytona, GMT-Master, and Submariner. Yet the Turn-O-Graph is a watch with a fascinating and significant history. Introduced in 1953, it was Rolex’s first commercially available watch with a rotating bezel—a feature often mistakenly credited to the Submariner—and the first sports model offered in Rolesor, the combination of steel and gold. By blending practical functionality with sporty elegance, the Turn-O-Graph laid the groundwork for what we now recognize as the modern tool watch. Its rotating bezel would go on to inspire defining features of some of Rolex’s most iconic sports watches, including the Submariner, and GMT-Master. Eventually, the Turn-O-Graph became integrated into the Datejust line, serving as its sporty variant. The example we have here is a classic 36 mm steel variant, featuring a turnable bezel in excellent condition and a beautifully preserved case. The stepped, pie-pan style silver dial is highlighted by striking black-topped hour markers, creating a sharp contrast and timeless appeal. It comes on a folded Jubilee bracelet, reference 6251H, with a clasp stamped “S W1” and end links marked 55. This sporty Datejust, complete with its slow-setting movement, has been fully serviced by our watchmaker and is ready to wear. A watch like this, with its silver Linen dial, turnable bezel, and sporty charm, doesn’t come around often. Contact us today to arrange a viewing or to find out more! description: The Rolex Turn-O-Graph ref. 6202, introduced in 1953, is often called the “grandfather” of the modern Rolex sports watch. While the Submariner receives most of the fame, the 6202 Turn-O-Graph was actually the first mass-produced Rolex to feature a rotating bezel. It established the design language later seen in the Submariner, GMT-Master, and the early Milgauss. Before the 6202, Rolex watches were mostly elegant Oyster Perpetuals; this model marked their first true “tool watch”. The 60-minute graduated bezel allowed users to track elapsed time, a revolutionary feature for professional timing at the time. title: Lemania Monopusher Chronograph 6BB Asymmetric Case Military Chronograph Black Dial issued to the Royal Air Force
description: Lemania is one of the most historically significant—and often overlooked—manufacturers of Swiss watch movements and chronographs. Founded in 1884, the company built an extraordinary reputation for precision engineering and complex watchmaking, producing legendary calibres that would eventually power watches used by NASA, military organizations and some of the world's most prestigious watch brands. The company was established in L’Orient, Switzerland, by Alfred Lugrin, who specialised in chronographs, stopwatches and repeating mechanisms. Lemania went on to become one of the great names in Swiss chronograph manufacturing, developing movements that earned a reputation for robustness, precision and reliability. In 1932, Lemania joined forces with Omega and Tissot under the newly created SSIH group (Société Suisse pour l’Industrie Horlogère), a structure that would become one of the major forces in Swiss watchmaking. Lemania chronographs became trusted instruments for military use, particularly for their reliability under demanding conditions. During the Cold War era, British military organisations, including the Royal Air Force and Special Forces, used Lemania chronographs, cementing the brand’s reputation for serious military-grade timekeeping. And this is exactly the kind of Lemania we love to find: an asymmetrical, single-pusher military chronograph in very good condition. The case is in fantastic condition, retaining all the little marks and traces of its hard military life. Rather than detracting from the watch, these honest signs of wear tell its story. The case back carries the correct military engravings a wonderful little detail for the collector. In keeping with British Ministry of Defence specifications, the matte black dial features both the Circle T marking, indicating the use of tritium luminous material, and the distinctive Broad Arrow. The dial itself is in great condition, with the original tritium still intact. Combined with the beautifully preserved military engravings and untouched character of the case, this is a wonderfully authentic piece of British military and watchmaking history. Honest, rugged and full of history. A proper military Lemania for the collector who appreciates watches with a story to tell , get in touch ! Thanks to its quartz movement, Audemars Piguet was able to reduce the case thickness to just 5.8 mm, creating an exceptionally elegant Royal Oak that slips effortlessly beneath a shirt cuff while retaining all of the collection's unmistakable design cues. The 33 mm 18 ct yellow gold case remains in excellent condition, with the original factory bevels and sharp lines beautifully preserved. The cream-coloured dial is wonderfully clean and features a finely printed railroad minute track, a date aperture at 3 o'clock, and beautifully aged cream-coloured lume on both the hour markers and hands. The warm patina complements the gold-printed Audemars Piguet signature perfectly, creating a harmonious and refined appearance. A sleeper in the Royal Oak world, don’t overlook this one!
